In the years since the Genocide Convention was signed in 1948, after the Nazi Holocaust, dozens of individuals have been successfully prosecuted for the crime of genocide, in conflicts such as those in Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia. But no state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide. Although the centuries-old practice has considerable potential for producing a wide range of contemporary goods, artisans say its survival depends on developing sustainable markets, supporting workshops and passing on their knowledge to younger generations. The craft, which involves transforming natural wool into a dense fabric through the application of water, soap and repeated rubbing and pressure, is among the oldest forms of textile production. Unlike woven fabrics, felt is made by interlocking wool fibers without the use of weaving or knitting. The process relies on the natural properties of wool and the skill and experience of the craftsperson. For generations, felt was used to make practical household items and clothing, particularly in communities where sheep farming provided an accessible source of raw material. Its insulating properties and durability made it suitable for different climates and everyday needs. Today, however, the craft is struggling to maintain its place in daily life, even as growing interest in traditional knowledge and handmade products offers opportunities for its revival. "For centuries, Christianity has been the world’s largest religion. That may soon change. Muslims are expected to outnumber Christians by 2035," the researchers said, noting that both groups are growing, but Muslims are growing faster. In 2020, the world had about 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims. "By 2070, if recent trends continue, there will be more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under 3 billion Christians worldwide," the center said. Muslims are expected to account for 36% of the population by then, up from 26% in 2020, while Christians will remain at around 29%. Hindus and Jews are projected to decline as a share of the global population, while Buddhists are expected to shrink both in number and proportion. "All other religions combined are expected to experience a modest increase in number," the researchers said. The projections assume that most global population growth in the 21st century will occur in Africa, the center added.

Li Ruikang Copied In international politics, the significance of a meeting is not always measured by the agreements reached, but sometimes by who are gathered around the table. When Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump sit down together in Shenzhen on Thursday, it will mark the first trilateral meeting among the leaders of the three major powers. The meeting will be held against the backdrop of conflict in many corners of the world, disruptions to energy supplies and supply chains, and excitement and concerns over new technologies and their regulation. Bringing the three leaders together creates an opportunity to communicate on issues that extend well beyond bilateral relationships. This does not mean the three countries will reach sweeping agreements or find common ground on every issue. However, the Shenzhen meeting is expected to establish a channel for strategic communication between the three powers, help reduce confrontation and improve their ability to manage differences. While the symbolism of the three leaders meeting together is high, analysts reject comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference, where the leaders of the United States, the Soviet Union and Britain negotiated key arrangements for the postwar world.

You can change your cookie settings through your browser. Ma Fengjie Copied A sore throat, a runny nose or an earache can disrupt an ordinary day. When symptoms become uncomfortable, some people reach for antibiotics left over from a previous illness, believing they will recover faster. But antibiotics do not work against every infection. If a sore throat is caused by a virus, for example, an antibiotic will not treat the cause. Unnecessary or incorrect use can have consequences far beyond one episode of illness. This everyday decision is connected to a much larger threat: antimicrobial resistance (AMR). As microorganisms become resistant to medicines designed to treat them, infections can become harder to cure. Antibiotic resistance is a major part of this challenge, threatening medicines on which modern healthcare depends. That is why World AMR Awareness Week, observed from November 18 to 24, matters to everyone. Its 2026 theme, "One Health, one action: Prevent AMR now," calls for coordinated action across human, animal and environmental health. World Children's Day on November 20, which falls during this week, reminds us that protecting children’s health also means using antibiotics wisely so that effective medicines remain available for future generations. China ranked first by a wide margin. Innovators based in China filed about 1.9 million patent applications, followed by the United States with 489,766, Japan with 466,301 and South Korea with 319,210. Asia accounted for 71.2% of global patent filings in 2025, up from 61.9% in 2015. China's strong growth was the main driver, with the country accounting for about 68.5% of all applications filed in Asia. In terms of technology fields, computer technology remained the largest area for patent applications in 2024, the latest year with complete data, accounting for 13% of published filings. Energy storage, particularly batteries, was the largest category among green technology patent applications, accounting for 17.4%. Smart energy, grids and power transmission followed with 15.2%, while air pollution control accounted for 11.8%.

Known as the Awa community, the indigenous group made their first contact in decades with a government team, requesting food for their group. The UK-based organisation Survival International released images from the contact on Tuesday. It described the contact as a "historic encounter" between a government team and around 20 members of the uncontacted community in Brazil's northeastern Maranhao state. The encounter took place on Monday. The organisation said such an approach was unusual, with no similar interaction involving the Awa reported in recent decades. It suggested that the group's request for food could be linked to increasing pressure from outsiders entering their territory. The Awa are a Tupi-Guarani Indigenous community living in north-western Maranhao, with some members continuing to live in voluntary isolation, according to Brazil's Indigenous affairs agency, Funai. The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation grouping is one of the few international bodies that include diplomatically isolated Taiwan, which China views as its own territory. Relations between Taipei and Beijing are extremely tense. China refuses to talk to Taiwan President Lai Ching-te, saying he is a ”separatist”, and its military operates around the island on a daily basis. Lai rejects Beijing’s sovereignty claims.
